Appointments to Boards and Commissions & Hiring

items.titleRaw: Ordinance 2026-29 – Amending the Bloomington Municipal Code to Prohibit the Development, Deployment, or Delivery of Superintelligence with the City of Bloomington, Indiana
items.summaryPlain: This ordinance would change Bloomington's city code to ban the development, deployment, or delivery of superintelligence within city limits.
items.decisionPlain: The council is reading this ordinance for the first time, which is an early step in the legislative process before any final decision is made.
items.publicCommentNote: First readings are typically read by title only; public comment on this item comes at its second reading.

items.titleRaw: Ordinance 2026-30 – Authorizing Issuance of City of Bloomington, Indiana, General Obligation Bonds, Series 2026, to Provide Funds to Finance the Costs of Certain Capital Improvements, and Equipping Projects and Incidental Expenses in
items.summaryPlain: This ordinance would allow the city to borrow money by issuing general obligation bonds to pay for capital improvements and equipment projects, along with related expenses and costs of issuing the bonds.
items.decisionPlain: The council is deciding whether to authorize the city to issue these bonds and to appropriate the money received from selling them.
items.publicCommentNote: First readings are typically read by title only; public comment on this item comes at its second reading.

items.titleRaw: Ordinance 2026-23 – UDO Amendments Related to Limited Compliance and Change in Use Standards
items.summaryPlain: This ordinance would change rules in the city's zoning code (called the UDO) that deal with 'limited compliance' and 'change in use standards' — these are regulations about what happens when properties don't fully meet current zoning requirements or when a property owner wants to use a building differently than it was used before.
items.decisionPlain: The council is doing a first reading of this ordinance, which means they are introducing it for initial review but not voting to approve it yet.
items.publicCommentNote: First readings are typically read by title only; public comment on this item comes at its second reading.

items.titleRaw: Appropriation Ordinance 2026-02 – An Ordinance for Appropriations and Tax Rates (Establishing 2027 Civil City Budget for the City of Bloomington)
items.summaryPlain: This is an ordinance that sets the City of Bloomington's overall budget and tax rates for the year 2027.
items.decisionPlain: The council is deciding whether to approve the city's spending plan and tax rates for 2027.
items.publicCommentNote: Public comment is taken on this item during the meeting before the vote.

items.titleRaw: Appropriation Ordinance 2026-04 – An Ordinance Adopting a Budget for the Operations, Maintenance, Debt Service, and Capital Improvements for the Water and Wastewater Utility Departments of the City of Bloomington, Indiana, for the Year 2027
items.summaryPlain: This ordinance sets the budget for the city's water and wastewater utility departments for 2027, covering their day-to-day operations, maintenance costs, debt payments, and capital improvement projects.
items.decisionPlain: The council is deciding whether to approve the 2027 budget for the water and wastewater utility departments.
items.publicCommentNote: Public comment is taken on this item during the meeting before the vote.

items.titleRaw: Ordinance 2026-21 – Updating Title 2 to Provide Better Apportionment of Representation on the Transportation Commission and Environment Commission
items.summaryPlain: This ordinance changes how members are distributed on two city commissions: the Transportation Commission and the Environment Commission.
items.decisionPlain: The council is deciding whether to approve changes to the city code that affect how representation is assigned on these two commissions.
items.publicCommentNote: Public comment is taken on this item during the meeting before the vote.

items.titleRaw: Ordinance 2026-22 – Prohibiting Use of Automated License Plate Reader (ALPR) Technology and Certain Video Surveillance Systems
items.summaryPlain: This ordinance would ban the city from using automated license plate reader technology and certain types of video surveillance systems.
items.decisionPlain: The council is deciding whether to pass this ordinance on its second reading, which would make it law if approved.
items.publicCommentNote: Public comment is taken on this item during the meeting before the vote.

items.titleRaw: Resolution 2026-22 – To Approve an Update to the City of Bloomington’s Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Transition Plan
items.summaryPlain: The city created a plan that identifies barriers preventing people with disabilities from accessing city facilities, programs, and services, and outlines how and when those barriers will be removed. This resolution would approve an updated version of that plan.
items.decisionPlain: The council is deciding whether to approve the updated Americans with Disabilities Act Transition Plan.
